package_info.package_versions: Orion Platform versions released between March 2020 and June 2020 (exact versions: 2019.4 HF 5, 2020.2 with HF 1 and HF 2)
package_info.why_malicious: Malicious code was surreptitiously injected into a core DLL of the SolarWinds Orion platform during the build process, resulting in a digitally signed, trojanized update that delivered a sophisticated backdoor (SUNBURST/Solorigate) to customer environments. This allowed attackers to gain persistent, covert access to thousands of organizations, including government and security industry targets.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (DLL load during Orion service startup)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Implements a covert backdoor that, upon loading the DLL, checks for network connectivity and anti-analysis conditions, then beacons to a remote command-and-control server. If a command is received, it executes attacker-supplied instructions on the victim system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code introduces network communications and remote command execution capabilities into a core business logic DLL, which is not expected in legitimate Orion software.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal business logic DLLs should not contain code for remote command-and-control, anti-analysis checks, or arbitrary command execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools may beacon to central servers, but not from core business logic DLLs and not with anti-analysis evasion.
key_indicators: Network beaconing from a business logic DLL
Code inserted in a digitally signed, trusted DLL

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to SolarWinds build infrastructure and injects malicious code into the Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll source or build process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is compiled and digitally signed as part of the official SolarWinds Orion release.

attack_chain.action: Trojanized DLL is distributed to customers via official SolarWinds update channels.
attack_chain.leads_to: Customers install the malicious update, loading the compromised DLL into their environments.

attack_chain.action: When the Orion service starts, the malicious DLL is loaded and the backdoor logic executes.
attack_chain.leads_to: Backdoor beacons to attacker-controlled infrastructure, awaiting further instructions.

attack_chain.action: Attacker issues commands to compromised systems via the backdoor, enabling lateral movement, data exfiltration, or further compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full attacker control of victim environments.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network communications from Orion business logic DLLs
Presence of anti-debugging or anti-sandbox logic in DLLs
Remote command execution capabilities in non-administrative components
Digitally signed binaries exhibiting C2 beaconing
file_indicators: Unexpected modifications to core Orion DLLs
DLLs with anomalous size or compile timestamps
network_indicators: Connections to known SUNBURST/Solorigate C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud[.]com)
Unusual outbound traffic from Orion servers to external IPs/domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected network activity originating from Orion platform processes, especially connections to known malicious C2 domains. Compare hashes and compile timestamps of core DLLs against trusted baselines. Analyze DLLs for anti-analysis logic and remote command execution code. Alert on any digitally signed SolarWinds DLLs exhibiting beaconing or C2 behavior.
